chunks.heading: What Does Types of Hail Damage in Snyder Properties Look Like?
chunks.text: Understanding different types of hail damage helps property owners recognize when professional assessment and repair are necessary.

chunks.heading: Asphalt Shingle Damage
chunks.text: Hail impacts create granule loss, exposed mat areas, cracking, and bruising. Small hail may only cause granule displacement, while large hail can crack or puncture shingles completely, requiring immediate replacement to prevent water intrusion.

chunks.heading: Metal Roofing Impact
chunks.text: Hail creates dents and dings in metal roofing systems that may not affect functionality immediately but can compromise coatings, leading to premature corrosion and reduced lifespan requiring professional evaluation and potential replacement.

chunks.heading: Flashing and Accessory Damage
chunks.text: Roof vents, flashing, gutters, and HVAC units often sustain visible denting from hail impacts. These components are critical for waterproofing and may require replacement even when primary roofing materials appear undamaged.

chunks.heading: Immediate vs. Progressive Damage
chunks.text: Some hail damage causes immediate leaks requiring post-storm documentation, while other damage compromises long-term integrity without immediate symptoms. Professional assessment identifies both types for comprehensive repair planning.

chunks.heading: Wind-Driven Hail Patterns
chunks.text: West Texas storms often combine hail with high winds, creating unique damage patterns on vertical surfaces and roof edges. These areas require special attention during assessment to ensure comprehensive damage identification.

chunks.heading: Interior Impact Assessment
chunks.text: Hail damage may cause interior water damage, ceiling stains, insulation damage, and electrical hazards. Comprehensive assessment includes interior inspection to document all related damage for insurance claims.

chunks.heading: Cost Per Square Foot: The Roofing Industry Standard
chunks.text: Roofing contractors typically price jobs by the "square" (100 square feet). Understanding this helps you evaluate quotes accurately:

chunks.heading: What a Proper Quote Should Include:
chunks.text: Detailed measurements (actual roof square footage) Material specifications (brand, model, color) Scope of work (tear-off, disposal, installation, cleanup) Warranty information (manufacturer and workmanship) Payment schedule Estimated timeline Itemized pricing (or at minimum, per-square pricing)

chunks.heading: Red Flags in Quotes:
chunks.text: Vague descriptions like "standard installation" No warranty information Requires large deposit (>30%) upfront Pressure to sign immediately Significantly lower than other quotes (often cut corners or use subpar materials)
